Article Title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei to AI companies: Fulfil your Cancer promise, rather than blaming me
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei dismissed calls for AI firms to rely on glossy campaigns

A rare, lengthy social media post

What comes next, according to Dario Amodei

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back against criticism that warnings about AI risks are fuelling public negativity. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Amodei said that the real issue is a ‘crisis of trust’ rooted in decades of suspicion toward companies, governments, and the tech industry. “Ordinary people don’t trust us and suspect we’re cooking up some new way to screw them over,” he wrote.Amodei dismissed calls for AI firms to rely on glossy campaigns to improve their image. “At this point, saying that AI will cure cancer is more a cliché than inspiring,” he said. Instead, he argued that the only way to rebuild trust is to actually deliver breakthroughs like curing cancer, rather than making promises that feel deceptive.Highlighting his own approach, Amodei said he is accountable to biomarkers and adjusts protocols based on measurable outcomes. He compared mastery in diet and health to excellence in academics, sports, or engineering, insisting that self‑control and discipline should be respected as legitimate forms of mastery.“I do agree that the public has a negative view of AI (and that this is a big problem), but I don’t think it is primarily caused by me or any other AI leader warning about AI’s risks.I think it is fundamentally a crisis of trust. I think that ordinary people don’t trust companies, governments, or the tech industry and always suspect that we are cooking up some new way to screw them over. The causes of this go back decades and AI is just the latest iteration of it. I don’t think that a glitzy marketing campaign with a positive spin (which some have advocated that Anthropic do) is the way to win back that trust — at this point, saying that AI will cure cancer is more a cliche than it is inspiring, and most people think it is deceptive. The thing that will work is *actually curing cancer*. I think by far the most accurate criticism of AI companies including Anthropic is that we haven’t yet delivered on our big promises to benefit the world. That is totally on us, and I think it’s the criticism you should be making, instead of all this stuff about messaging and marketing”, wrote Amodei on X.Amodei laid out his argument in an extended post on X on Saturday, a platform he generally avoids, according to a Fortune report. He began by addressing the debate around AI regulation, describing what he sees as a false choice between critics who worry regulation leads to concentrated corporate power and those who argue that widely distributing AI, including through open-weight models, is the better safeguard. Amodei argued that institutions like the court system show power can be decentralized without abandoning oversight, and noted that Anthropic has backed policies that would slow down frontier AI companies like itself while giving smaller competitors more room to operate.He acknowledged that AI does tend to concentrate power structurally, but attributed that tendency to the scaling laws underlying how AI models improve as more computing resources are put into them, rather than to regulation itself. In his view, open-weight models only shift that concentration toward whoever controls the most computing capacity and chips, rather than eliminating it. He said he favors "rules of the road" that address AI's cyber, biological and alignment risks while also institutionally constraining the power of frontier AI companies and leaving room for open-weight models, and voiced support for a FINRA-like regulatory body as well as the Trump administration's approach to AI testing.Amodei said Anthropic is trying to rebuild credibility by producing tangible results, pointing specifically to increased work in biology and medicine, and describing "early glimmers" of what he suggested could eventually be significant breakthroughs. Until there are actual accomplishments to point to, he said the company would avoid making further big promises and instead focus on being transparent about AI's risks in the meantime, arguing that honesty carries no more public credibility risk, and quite possibly less, than an approach that downplays or distracts from risks people already sense are real.
Article Summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has pushed back against criticism that warnings about AI risks are fuelling public negativity. ‘Ordinary people don’t trust us and suspect we’re cooking up some new way to screw them over,’ he wrote. He dismissed calls for AI firms to rely on glossy campaigns to improve their image.

Article Title: When 'Godfather of AI' agreed with Elon Musk; said billionaires like him are right about future of work; but there is a big problem and that is...
Article Text:
Geoffrey Hinton says Musk and Gates are right about AI ending jobs, but warns the real problem is nobody left to buy what AI makes.

Why Geoffrey Hinton thinks the trillion-dollar AI spending spree runs on job cuts

AI will create new jobs, but Hinton says nowhere near enough to replace what it kills

Bernie Sanders warns 100 million US jobs face AI automation risk

Geoffrey Hinton and Elon Musk do not usually land on the same side of an argument. But asked whether the tech billionaires forecasting the end of work were being melodramatic, the Nobel laureate widely called the "Godfather of AI" said they were probably right. Musk has said most people won't have to work at all inside two decades. Similarly, Bill Gates has suggested humans may soon not be needed for most things. Hinton, in a discussion with Senator Bernie Sanders last year at Georgetown University, said those predictions are not fringe. They are likely.The catch is everything that follows. Hinton's worry is not that AI is bad technology. It is that the economy sitting underneath it was not built to absorb what is coming. He expects "massive unemployment caused by AI", and he does not think the people writing the cheques have worked through the consequences. His blunt line to Sanders was that if workers stop earning, "there's nobody to buy their products".Follow the money, Hinton argued, and the intent becomes obvious. Somebody has to recover the roughly trillion dollars flowing into data centres and chips, and subscription fees for chatbots won't cover it. The return has to come from selling companies AI that does a worker's job for less. Big Tech, in his reading, is betting squarely on replacement. The financial pressure is real enough: HSBC estimated OpenAI won't turn a profit before 2030 and may need over $207 billion to keep scaling.Hinton also keeps pointing out that this is a design choice, not destiny. AI could do enormous good in healthcare and education. What makes it dangerous is distribution. Musk gets richer, a lot of people lose work, and as Hinton put it, "that's on how we organize society".The standard rebuttal is that every technology shock eventually produces new categories of work. Hinton accepts the first half and rejects the second. Yes, roles like prompt engineer appear. No, he does not believe they arrive in anything like the volume of the jobs being erased. The old escape route mattered: a ditch digger could move to a call centre. Those call centre desks are the ones going first.He is careful about his own confidence, though. Predicting AI, he told Sanders, is like driving in fog, where the next hundred yards are clear and the two hundred yard mark is invisible. A year or two out, he can see. Ten years out, nobody can. At the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas this month, he went further on capability, saying AI could surpass humans at everything within twenty years, and probably a good deal sooner.Sanders has tried to size the damage. An report last year from his office estimated nearly 100 million US jobs are exposed to automation, covering fast food, customer service and manual labour, but also accounting, software development and nursing. Senator Mark Warner has warned recent graduates could face unemployment near 25% within three years.Hinton's fog is still there. The 175,479 tech jobs cut in this year are not, and the names on that list run through Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Oracle, and plenty of others.
Article Summary: Geoffrey Hinton says the real problem is nobody left to buy what AI makes. Musk has said most people won't have to work at all inside two decades. Bill Gates has suggested humans may soon not be needed for most things. Hinton accepts the first half and rejects the second.

Article Title: America is 'getting ready' to send letter to dozens of countries telling them: You can go with us or China, it cannot be ...
Article Text:
America to send letter to dozens of countries

‘To be part of everything is to be part of nothing’

The Chinese alternative

Why Washington is pushing this now

The United States is preparing to send a letter to dozens of countries, telling them that they must choose sides in the global AI race, according to a report by Reuters. As per a US official and a draft reviewed by Reuters, nations that join China’s competing framework will be excluded from Washington’s coalition, known as Pax Silica. For the uninitiated, launched last year, Pax Silica is designed to secure supply chains for AI models, semiconductors and critical minerals. Around two dozen countries have signed on, including Japan, Australia, South Korea, and Kazakhstan. But Kazakhstan has also joined China’s newly announced World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, raising concerns in Washington. The draft letter warns: “To be part of everything is to be part of nothing. Signature of the Pax Silica Declaration is not merely a membership subscription, but a commitment.”As per the report, The draft letter, prepared by the State Department, is addressed to the 35 signatories of a US. "AI Opportunity Statement" signed in June. Those signatories include members of the non-binding Pax Silica framework, an initiative Washington launched last year aimed at securing supply chains for AI models, semiconductors and critical minerals amid its intensifying rivalry with Beijing, as well as other countries that have expressed interest in aligning their AI cooperation with the US.Roughly two dozen countries have already joined Pax Silica, including close US. allies such as Japan, Australia and South Korea, along with Kazakhstan, a key potential source of critical minerals. Kazakhstan's involvement has drawn particular attention in Washington because it is also the only country known to have joined China's rival coalition, a dual membership that Reuters reports has set off alarm bells among US officials.The draft letter makes the case that AI alignment cannot be treated as a flexible, à la carte arrangement. It states that "to be part of everything is to be part of nothing," framing signature on the Pax Silica declaration as a genuine commitment rather than a simple membership subscription, and urging countries to choose deliberately rather than trying to straddle both camps. Without naming China explicitly, the letter argues that Pax Silica membership cannot be held alongside participation in duplicative initiatives whose expectations conflict with Washington's own. Reuters was unable to determine when the letter might actually be sent, or whether its language could still change beforehand, since the draft reviewed was undated.The letter is a direct response to a rival framework China has been building. In July, Chinese President Xi Jinping launched the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, positioning the country's open-weight AI technology as a challenge to US. dominance in the sector. The move reflects a broader shift in the global AI landscape, as Chinese open-weight models have made rapid gains against proprietary systems built by US. companies like OpenAI and Anthropic, intensifying the stakes of the broader technological rivalry.By pressing allied and partner countries to pick a side, the US. is aiming to limit China's access to resources in the broader race to build the most advanced AI systems, technology that could carry significant military and economic weight. Pax Silica itself is designed to push US. allies toward joint projects and coordinated export controls while reducing collective reliance on adversaries for critical minerals, AI models and the semiconductor chips that power them.The critical minerals dimension adds further weight to the standoff. China has previously used its near-monopoly over several critical minerals as leverage in a tariff dispute launched last year by President Donald Trump, who has since pushed to expand domestic and allied sourcing of those materials. Kazakhstan's June entry into Pax Silica was touted by Washington as a milestone, marking the first Central Asian country to join the framework and bringing with it substantial reserves of critical minerals central to advanced technology supply chains.Under the current structure, Pax Silica members gain access to shared investment opportunities in AI-related projects, while countries that have simply signed the AI Opportunity Statement have made a more symbolic commitment to a shared vision and common purpose with the US, according to the statement posted on the State Department's website. A US official told Reuters that the letter was drafted specifically to make clear that countries can't have it both ways, arguing that it is difficult for any nation to credibly present itself as a trusted partner within one technology ecosystem while simultaneously joining an initiative built by China to advance a competing vision for AI.
Article Summary: US preparing to send letter to dozens of countries, telling them that they must choose sides in the global AI race. The letter is a direct response to a rival framework China has been building. In July, Chinese President Xi Jinping launched the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, positioning the country's open-weight AI technology.

Article Title: Tech millionaire Bryan Johnson hits back at ‘eating disorder’ claims: ‘I’ve achieved perfect discipline’
Article Text:
What Bryan Johnson said

Data‑driven accountability

Read Byran Johnson’s complete post here

‘People say I have an eating disorder.

Because I've achieved perfect discipline of what I eat. It's taken me years to achieve this mastery.

Yet the reaction is to call it a disorder.

Should a straight A student get some Bs, Cs and Ds to avoid having a grade disorder?

Should an NBA player miss some shots to avoid having a shooting disorder?

Should an engineer introduce some bugs in the code to avoid having a code disorder?

We celebrate mastery of craft in other domains. Why not what we put into our bodies?

I'm accountable to my biomarkers and change the protocol according to the data.

Like any quest for mastery, this one can steer into unhealthy territory. But self control over food intake is as worthy of respect as mastery of any other craft.’

Anti-aging influencer and tech millionaire Bryan Johnson has reignited a long-running public debate over his relationship with food, posting on X that he rejects being told he has an eating disorder, arguing instead that what critics see as pathology is actually years of disciplined mastery over what he eats. “People say I have an eating disorder. Because I've achieved perfect discipline of what I eat. It's taken me years to achieve this mastery,” Johnson wrote, questioning why mastery in food intake is often pathologised when excellence in other fields is celebrated.In the post, Johnson wrote that people accuse him of having an eating disorder because he has achieved what he describes as perfect discipline in his diet, something he says took years to build. He questioned why that discipline gets labeled a disorder rather than celebrated as skill, drawing comparisons to other domains where extreme consistency is praised rather than pathologized: a straight-A student isn't told to get some Cs to avoid a "grade disorder," he argued, an NBA player isn't told to miss shots to avoid a "shooting disorder," and an engineer isn't told to introduce bugs to avoid a "code disorder." He said he holds himself accountable to his biomarkers and adjusts his health protocol based on data, while acknowledging that any pursuit of mastery, including this one, can tip into unhealthy territory. Even so, he maintained that self-control over food intake deserves the same respect as mastery of any other craft.Johnson emphasised that his approach is not rigid dogma but biomarker‑driven. He said he continually adjusts his protocol based on measurable health data, treating food intake as a craft worthy of respect. “Like any quest for mastery, this one can steer into unhealthy territory. But self‑control over food intake is as worthy of respect as mastery of any other craft,” he concluded.
Article Summary: Bryan Johnson has reignited a long-running public debate over his relationship with food. He wrote that he rejects being told he has an eating disorder, arguing instead that what critics see as pathology is actually years of disciplined mastery over what he eats. He questioned why that discipline gets labeled a disorder rather than celebrated as skill.

Article Title: ChatGPT gave Google 'Code Red’, prompting co-founder Sergey Brin's return; Now OpenAI’s Greg Brockman is facing 'Red Flag'
Article Text:
Greg Brockman goes into ‘founder mode’

OpenAI witnessing a wave of high-profile departures

In December 2022, the meteoric rise of ChatGPT reportedly triggered a “Code Red” inside Google . The situation led co-founder Sergey Brin back into hands-on technical development. Fast forward to August 2026, the tables have turned, presenting OpenAI leadership led by CEO Sam Altman and president Greg Brockman (both cofounders) with what industry analysts are calling a major “red flag” of their own.A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the AI company’s front office at a critical juncture, as the artificial intelligence (AI) giant prepares for an anticipated initial public offering ( IPO ) while seeking to validate an $852 billion valuation.Meanwhile, citing sources familiar to the matter, a report by Axios claims that Brockman is getting more involved in the company’s day-to-day operations to contain disruptions. Brockman is said to be meeting with more customers and teams across the company than ever before. Brockman is said to be publicly framing the departures as a change in corporate focus.The latest blow came with the resignation of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser after less than a year at the company. Dresser, a seasoned software executive who previously spent over a decade at Salesforce and Slack, was recruited in December to spearhead OpenAI's enterprise commercial strategy against formidable rivals like Anthropic.Her departure landed just two days after longtime COO and senior executive, Brad Lightcap, announced his own exit after eight years, leaving key corporate divisions in transition. Her profile expanded significantly four months later when she took over operational duties previously handled by Lightcap. However, Dresser's abrupt departure compounds a broader pattern of senior leadership churn.For example, Fidji Simo, the former Instacart CEO stepped away from her high-ranking OpenAI executive role in July to focus on managing a chronic illness. Four other senior leaders, including former VP of Science Kevin Weil and CMO Kate Rouch, left the company in April. The exits arrive only months after OpenAI submitted a confidential IPO draft registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission, raising concerns among private market watchers.“The executives leaving OpenAI ahead of their IPO is a huge red flag,” noted Kevin McCormick, founder of AI startup SignAudit.AI, pointing out that walking away before a liquidity event suggests underlying tensions.“If the executives leaving aren’t being ‘made whole’ by the next company, it’s bad news for OpenAI,” McCormick wrote, as per a report by CNBC.Meanwhile, Dali Rajic – former COO of cybersecurity firm Wiz – joined as chief revenue officer. OpenAI also hired top AI researcher Noam Shazeer from Google in June 2026. He is a co-inventor of the foundational transformer architecture and former co-lead of Google’s Gemini models, and joined OpenAI to head Architecture Research.
Article Summary: A wave of high-profile executive departures is shaking the AI company’s front office at a critical juncture. The exits arrive only months after OpenAI submitted a confidential IPO draft registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The latest blow came with the resignation of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser.

Article Title: ‘10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints, non-delivery of goods top grievance; Rs 91 crore refunds in one year’
Article Text:
​10 online shopping platforms that faced most consumer complaints

Top 10 E-Commerce Platforms by Grievance Volume

Regulatory crackdown and refunds

How NCH complaint system works

Online shopping giants Flipkart, Amazon and Meesho emerged as the top three platforms facing the highest volume of consumer grievances on the National Consumer Helpline (NCH) in 2025, the government informed the Lok Sabha recently. In a written reply to the Parliament, Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs BL Verma disclosed that Flipkart topped the list with over 1.33 lakh complaints, followed by Amazon with 91,248 and Meesho with 29,284. Quick-commerce and niche retail platforms also featured prominently among the top ten offenders.Operated by the Department of Consumer Affairs, the NCH acts as a single-window pre-litigation website. It currently supports 17 Indian languages and connects consumers with 1,853 partner companies registered under its voluntary "Convergence" initiative. This means that consumers can lodge complaints in 17 languages, including Hindi, English, Kashmiri, Punjabi, Nepali, Gujarati, Marathi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Maithili, Santhali, Bengali, Odia, Assamese and Manipuri, through the toll-free number 1915.* Flipkart: 1,33,000* Amazon: 91,248* Meesho: 29,284* Myntra: 25,384* Netmeds: 19,895* Zepto: 5,774* Blinkit: 5,102* Naaptol: 4,079* VLE Bazaar: 3,907* Nykaa: 3,405To curb unfair trade practices under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposed fines on 47 platforms, slapping collective fines totaling approximately Rs 1.12 crore (Rs 1,12,01,500). The minister highlighted significant enforcement outcomes through pre-litigation resolution.The minister said that the NCH facilitated refunds of over Rs 91 crore to consumers between April 25, 2025, and June 30, 2026, of which more than Rs 63 crore pertained to grievances in the e-commerce sector. This was achieved by resolving over 1,47,000 consumer grievances related to refund claims at the pre-litigation stage, he said. A total of 5.11 lakh complaints related to quick commerce were received on the NCH in 2025, all of which were disposed of, the minister added.Non-delivery of products was the single largest category of complaints in 2025, accounting for 79,818 cases. Other frequent complaints included delivery of the wrong product, denial of replacement or refund as per policy, delivery of defective or damaged goods, non-refund of paid amounts, deficiency in services, sale of spurious or counterfeit products, and unauthorised debit of amounts without consumer consent.Consumers can escalate unresolved e-commerce disputes through:* Toll-Free Helpline: 1915* WhatsApp / SMS: 8800001915* Email: nch-ca@gov.in* Complaint websites: consumerhelpline.gov.in, the NCH app, and the UMANG application

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of…”
Article Text:
Image: AP News

Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos

“I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.”

What does this quote mean?

Limitations can force us to think differently

Necessity has a long history of creating innovation

Frugality can make innovation more efficient

Constraints can turn problems into creative challenges

Creativity often grows outside the comfort zone

Why this quote still matters today

Innovation is often associated with having more, more money, more resources, more advanced technology and more time. But some of the most creative solutions emerge when those advantages are limited. Jeff Bezos captured this idea when he said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out.” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress. Sometimes, they force people to think differently, question familiar methods and find solutions that would never have emerged in more comfortable circumstances.Jeff Bezos (1964-present) is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He built the company from an online bookseller into one of the world's largest technology and e-commerce businesses and has also pursued ventures in space exploration through Blue Origin. His observation highlights how constraints can turn necessity into a catalyst for experimentation and inventive thinking.This statement implies that scarcity of resources can be an impetus for innovation. When there are no simple solutions, people are obliged to rethink how to do things. Tight budget, shortage of materials, or technical difficulties can become the grounds for experimenting rather than excuses for inaction. The main message that Bezos tries to convey here is that constraints can make people innovative.In the case of abundance of resources, it is easy to find a solution by adding more resources, people, tools or funds. Constraints take away that luxury. All of a sudden, efficiency becomes the priority, and common assumptions should be questioned. A constrained team might discover a simpler way of doing things just because they do not have enough means to operate according to the traditional way.Useful innovations have often been developed due to people’s needs for solving certain problems using what was already available at hand. In cases ranging from simple farming implements to sophisticated medical gadgets that operate in conditions of limited resources, necessity has proved time and again to breed creativity. In the absence of an apparent solution, people start to search for other ways of solving their problems.Innovation does not necessarily mean that you should develop something that is larger or more complicated than your current product. Some of the most outstanding solutions come when people try to do the same thing using less material resources or reducing superfluous steps in a process. This way, frugality may become another incentive for inventors to find what really matters.It may seem as if a hard constraint makes the issue a roadblock. However, perceiving a limitation as a challenge will make a difference in the mindset when it comes to dealing with an issue. The question from “Why can't we do this?” will turn into “How could we do this differently?” This approach can foster experimenting and coming up with unique ideas.Comfort can help one to carry on with the things as usual. Constraints break up the sense of comfort. They make one think and come up with new options. Regardless of whether one is starting a business, developing a product or even solving a simple problem, constraints can provide a different perspective of creativity than abundance can.Whether it be startups trying to innovate on meager resources or scientists innovating the technology to suit a harsh environment, innovations often emerge when there is a sense of urgency involved. The words of Jeff Bezos provide an excellent point that lack of resources should not necessarily translate into lack of opportunities. In some cases, the very fact that there is no easy way out leads to innovation of a solution. The lesson from the statement is quite straightforward: Innovation occurs when nothing else works.
Article Summary: Jeff Bezos is an American entrepreneur and founder of Amazon. He said, “I think frugality drives innovation, just like other constraints do. One of the only ways to get out of a tight box is to invent your way out” His words suggest that limitations do not always prevent progress.

Article Title: How Google's parent Alphabet turned into the biggest profitable shareholder after SpaceX's IPO
Article Text:
A historic return on venture capital

Concentration among top institutional backers

Fidelity investments is ranked as the second-largest institutional shareholder with 302.6 million shares.

Gigafund management reported holding 171.8 million shares.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) disclosed a 154.1 million-share position valued at $26.3 billion at the end of the second quarter.

Baillie Gifford & BlackRock reported stakes of 51.4 million and 51.0 million shares, respectively.

Other major holders include Brookfield Corp. with 19.2 million shares, Hancock Prospecting with 8 million shares valued at $1.4 billion, Balyasny Asset Management with 3.4 million shares, and Tiger Global Management holding 375,000 shares.

Alphabet’s decade-old gamble on Elon Musk’s space company has delivered a lucrative return, turning Google’s parent company into the largest institutional shareholder following SpaceX’s blockbuster initial public offering (IPO). Citing quarterly regulatory disclosures, news agency Reuters reports that Alphabet held a position valued at approximately $94.2 billion at the end of June. The valuation stems from an original $900 million investment made in SpaceX back in 2015 – representing a huge gain of more than 100 times its starting capital.SpaceX completed an $86 billion public listing in June, providing the first clear public window into the enormous stakes accumulated by early institutional backers while the rocket and satellite company operated as a private startup.According to Alphabet’s second-quarter 13F regulatory filing, the tech giant held 551.2 million SpaceX shares as of June 30, when the aerospace manufacturer was trading at $170.86 per share. Even with normal post-IPO stock fluctuations adjusting the market value of the position to around $77.9 billion by mid-August, Alphabet’s holding still stands at roughly 86.5 times the size of its initial 2015 check.Market analysts noted that while tracking precise institutional entry prices across multiple funding rounds is challenging, Alphabet’s publicly documented $900 million transaction in 2015 offers a clear baseline illustrating how private-market aerospace valuation translated into massive public market gains, the report added.The latest round of regulatory filings also outlines the broader distribution of SpaceX shares across global asset managers and sovereign wealth funds.
Article Summary: Alphabet is the largest institutional shareholder of SpaceX, according to regulatory filings. Fidelity investments is ranked as the second-largest institutional shareholder with 302.6 million shares. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) disclosed a 154.1 million-share position valued at $26.3 billion at the end of June.

Jensen Huang-led Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest as much as $3 billion in SB Energy, a SoftBank Group subsidiary developing ‌a massive planned Ohio data center project for OpenAI, reports The Information citing people familiar with the discussions. It ​is building several data center campuses to ​support rising ⁠demand tied to AI workloads.The Wall Street Journal reported last week that Nvidia had scaled back its Ohio guarantee to under $120 billion, down from an earlier $250 billion figure.In another news, Nvidia has disclosed that it owns nearly 123 million shares in SpaceX, the space company owned by Elon Musk.The stake was worth almost $21 billion at the end of June, but has since fallen to about $17 billion as SpaceX shares dropped sharply following its June initial public offering.The disclosure sheds light on Nvidia’s investment in xAI, which was completed in January, shortly before Musk combined the AI lab with SpaceX. It also highlights Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s efforts to use the financial strength of the $5.5 trillion company to build financial links across the AI industry, including with some of its biggest customers.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jensen Huang, ‘The more you buy, the more you save’
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jensen Huang

What Jensen Huang's quote means

Why the line resonates (and gets mocked)

Applying the idea beyond semiconductors

A simple takeaway

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the company at the center of the global AI boom, with Nvidia's GPUs now powering everything from video games to the largest AI models in the world. Along the way, Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes. Few have generated as much discussion, and as much good-natured mockery, as this one."The more you buy, the more you save."On its face, the quote sounds like it inverts basic financial logic — spending more money is not usually how anyone ends up saving money. Huang himself has acknowledged the tension directly, once following the line up by calling it "CEO math," adding that it's "not accurate, but it is correct." That qualifier is doing a lot of work. He isn't claiming the arithmetic checks out in a literal sense. He's arguing that from a strategic, systems-level view, larger upfront investment in the right infrastructure can produce disproportionate long-term returns, even if the sticker price climbs.The context matters here. Huang has used the line specifically to describe investment in Nvidia's GPU and networking infrastructure for AI data centers. His argument is that building at scale, investing heavily in accelerated computing rather than trying to get by with smaller, incremental upgrades, ultimately reduces the total cost and energy required to do the same amount of computing work. In other words, the "saving" isn't in the sense of holding onto more cash today. It's in the efficiency gained per unit of computation once the larger system is up and running.Part of what makes the quote memorable is exactly the tension it plays with. It sounds like a walking cliché of corporate spin, the kind of thing said to justify a big expense after the fact. That's precisely why it's been widely shared, sometimes sincerely as an illustration of infrastructure economics, and sometimes as a punchline, including consumer tech outlets jokingly applying the phrase to PC-building shopping sprees that were anything but frugal.But there's a real principle underneath the joke. In large-scale computing, cost efficiency often doesn't scale linearly. A company that invests in a fully built-out, high-performance system can end up paying less per unit of useful output than one that buys smaller, cheaper components piecemeal and stitches them together inefficiently. Huang's framing asks decision-makers to evaluate cost per outcome rather than sticker price in isolation, a shift in thinking that applies well beyond chips and data centers.The logic behind "CEO math" shows up in other investment decisions too, when approached carefully. Buying a higher-quality tool or system upfront, one built to handle a job well rather than just adequately, can reduce the long-run cost of inefficiency, breakdowns, or having to redo work later. The same reasoning applies to hiring, education, or infrastructure of almost any kind: the cheapest option today isn't automatically the cheapest option over time.The caveat, and it's an important one, is that this logic only holds when the larger investment is actually well-targeted. Spending more without a clear efficiency payoff isn't strategic, it's just spending more. Huang's own framing depends entirely on the assumption that the additional expense buys genuine capability and efficiency gains, not simply a bigger price tag.The quote works best as a prompt to look past the initial cost of a decision and ask what it actually buys in terms of long-term value. The next time a larger upfront investment feels wasteful on the surface, the more useful question isn't "is this expensive?" but "does this genuinely reduce cost or increase output per dollar over time?" Huang's line is deliberately provocative precisely because it forces that question into the open, even while admitting, with a wink, that the math doesn't quite add up the way it sounds.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has spent more than three decades steering it from a scrappy graphics chip maker into the center of the global AI boom. Huang has developed a reputation not just for technical vision but for blunt, often counterintuitive one-liners delivered on stage at Nvidia's keynotes.

Article Title: US Immigration authority to H1-B visa holders, students and other visa holders: These forms will be rejected starting September 15
Article Text:
USCIS says no grace period will be available for Form I-539 and Form I-765 change

What are Form I-539 and Form I-765

USCIS says no grace period for form change

“If filing Form I-539, please note that USCIS will:

Accept the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-539 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026.

If filing Form I-765, please note that USCIS will:

Accept the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted before Sept. 15, 2026;

Reject the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026; and

Only accept the 09/15/26 edition of Form I-765 if it is postmarked or electronically submitted on or after Sept. 15, 2026."

The US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that two of its important immigration forms will be replaced with new editions, starting September 15. The change will be applicable to Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26). The agency further stated that from September 15, it will only accept the 09/15/26 editions of these forms, clarifying that applications with old forms will get rejected. In its official announcement, the immigration authority said that the revised forms “align with the recently published Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors, and Representatives of Foreign Information Media final rule”.“On Sept. 15, 2026, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will publish revised editions of Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and Form I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26),” the agency said adding “The 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 replace the 08/28/24 edition of Form I-539 and the 08/21/25 edition of Form I-765”.Used by H-1B visa holders, students and other visa holders, the I-539 form is for immigration status, while the I-765 form is for work authorization.Form I-539: Used to extend or change a nonimmigrant visa status while in the US. The H-1B worker does not use I-539 to extend or change H-1B status. The employer generally files Form I-129. However, H-1B dependents (H-4 spouses and children) can use I-539 to extend or change their status.Form I-765: Used to apply for work permission, also known as an Employment Authorization Document (EAD). An H-1B worker generally does not use I-765 for their H-1B work authorization. However, certain H-4 spouses may use I-765 to apply for an Employment Authorization Document (EAD), if they meet the eligibility requirements.In the announcement, USCIS further clarifies that there is no grace period for the revised editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 because the revised editions are necessary for USCIS to apply the final rule.“Because there will be no grace period, USCIS is providing preview versions of the 09/15/26 editions of Form I-539 and Form I-765 with their instructions. Do not file the 09/15/26 editions of these forms before Sept. 15, 2026,” the immigration agency stated.Here’s what the agency says
Article Summary: US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has announced that two of its important immigration forms will be replaced with new editions, starting September 15. The change will be applicable to Form I-539, Application to Extend/Change Nonimmigrant Status, and forms I-765, Application for Employment Authorization (edition date for both: 09/15/26)

Article Title: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart after food safety checks
Article Text:
Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration suspends 14 licences linked to Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart after food safety checks

Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart licences suspended

Zepto outlet in Pune found with expired food

Blinkit facilities flagged over temperature, hygiene

Zepto and Instamart outlets face food storage violations

The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the licences of 14 food businesses linked to quick-commerce platforms Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. According to a report by PTI, the inspection drive covered 86 establishments involved in storing, selling and delivering food through online platforms. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene, food safety records and compliance with required food handling practices.As reported by PTI, the FDA also issued 60 improvement notices and directed one facility to temporarily stop operations, the news agency stated.Of the 14 suspended licences, five were linked to Blinkit, five to Zepto and two to Instamart. One licence each was suspended for Bhagwati Stores and Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd. The FDA said its inspections focused on whether food businesses were following prescribed safety and hygiene rules while storing and handling products.Officials checked storage conditions, temperature control, cleanliness, pest management and personal hygiene of food workers.They also checked food safety records, display of licences and inventory systems such as First In, First Out (FIFO) and First Expired, First Out (FEFO).In Pune, the FDA suspended the licence of a Zepto outlet in Lohegaon after inspectors found food products stored beyond their declared "use by" dates. Officials also found unhygienic storage conditions, inadequate pest control and lapses in the personal hygiene of workers. The FDA said the response given by the company during the hearing was unsatisfactory.Another Pune facility operated by Swinsta Ent Pvt Ltd was found to have a cockroach infestation. Inspectors also reported problems with cold-chain maintenance for frozen products and deficiencies in hygiene and pest control.A Blinkit facility in Malad, Mumbai, was found operating with chiller temperatures above the prescribed limit. The FDA also found that around 40 food handlers had not undergone mandatory medical examinations, and the required records were not available.Officials further found that some workers were not using protective equipment such as gloves, aprons and head coverings. Damaged storage racks, poor organisation and inadequate separation of different food categories were also reported.At another Blinkit facility in Ghatkopar, inspectors found issues involving drainage, waste disposal, temperature control and housekeeping. The outlet scored 46% during the inspection and was classified as non-compliant.Inspections at Zepto facilities in Mulund and Goregaon found deficiencies related to food storage, temperature management, cleanliness and licence display. At an Instamart outlet in Andheri, inspectors found food packets stored directly on the floor. The FDA also reported inadequate storage space, overcrowding and problems with hygiene and temperature control.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has suspended licences of 14 food businesses linked to Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart. The development comes after a statewide inspection drive on August 13 that found several food safety and hygiene violations. The inspections covered food storage, temperature control, cleanliness, pest control, worker hygiene and compliance with required food handling practices.
